text:
Jaden Schwartz played his college hockey at Colorado College, won a Cup with St. Louis in 2019, spent four seasons in Seattle and is now, at 34, a depth scorer for the Avalanche. It's working so far: 7 goals and 14 points in 23 games on under 14 minutes a night.

The goals deserve a careful look. He has 7 on 3.9 expected, shooting 18% against 13% last season. The chances are real, and his shot is still among the hardest in the league (top 7% by speed), but that finishing rate rarely lasts. At five on five, Colorado gets about 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, four points worse than when he sits.

What he gives them is a different look. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting his own zone with possession 67% of the time last season, and more than half his shots came off the rush. Evolving-Hockey noted he spent last season with some of the weakest teammates in the league, bottom 1%. That's no longer his problem. We'd watch whether the goals keep coming once the shooting cools.
